tasks.short: Walk patrol rounds on the premises, check doors, windows and gates, and deal with what is found.

steps.what: Security guard patrols the premises, checking doors, windows and gates and scanning checkpoints
Security guard notes findings such as an open door or broken light
Security guard secures what can be secured or phones the site contact
Control room operator checks the round was completed in the guard tour log
Facility manager reads the findings and orders repairs

tasks.design: Configure the guard tour system ({OTHER}) so a checkpoint scan opens a finding form with location filled in, a finding type list and a photo. Non-urgent findings become work orders in the facility {HELPDESK} automatically, and the control room sees live round progress with an alert for missed checkpoints.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guard tour devices only logged checkpoint times; findings went on paper and by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Guard tour apps on phones take photos and forms, and helpdesks accept work orders by e-mail or interface.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting signs of intrusion is the guard's eye on site; walking the round takes the same time.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing what is out of place on a site they know, and acting safely when something is wrong.

ambition.what: Patrol routes and times adjusted every month from the finding history, not fixed for the contract term.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; findings reach the facility manager without a phone call.

reach.learn: Whether finding types match the repair categories facilities uses.

evidence.claim: Guard tour apps can attach forms and photos to checkpoint scans.
Tools that record a person's movements at work can observe performance, so the works council must consent in the Netherlands.
Private security organisations need a licence and screened staff in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Boundary: from the start of a round to findings handled or passed on; repairs are outside.

Input contract: checkpoint IDs and locations set up by the security supervisor in the guard tour system; finding types agreed by the supervisor and facility manager; fallback is paper notes and a call.
Round logs show completion per round, not individual pace, unless the works council agrees.
Control room and facility manager time is outside the guard's savings.
unknowns: Whether the guard tour system supports forms and photos.
How many findings a round produces.
research_questions: How long do findings wait for repair today?

already_counted.description: Guard confirms the checkpoint location and picks the finding type in the app.

incremental.description: Guard replaces damaged checkpoint tags and reports app faults.
Security supervisor maintains checkpoints and finding types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Quiet sites with few findings save only seconds per round; the walk itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Respond to alarms, investigate the cause on site, call help if needed, reset and report the outcome.

steps.what: Control room operator receives alarms and dispatches the guard to answer them
Security guard goes to the alarm location
Security guard investigates disturbances: checks area, camera images, people present
Security guard decides: false alarm, reset, call emergency services or escalate
Security guard phones police, fire service or the key holder when needed
Security guard resets the alarm and radios the outcome to the control room
Control room operator logs the alarm and outcome in the alarm log

tasks.design: Link the alarm system ({OTHER}) to a dispatch app on the guard's phone: each alarm arrives with zone map, last camera snapshot and key-holder list, and the guard closes it with an outcome code and short note that write straight to the alarm log. Calls to emergency services and key holders are one tap from the same screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alarm systems, radios and the alarm log were separate, so every outcome was told by radio and typed again.
tasks.enabler_now: Alarm platforms expose events to apps, and phone apps can show maps, snapshots and forms.
tasks.still_hard: Going to the scene and judging what happened is risky, human work; camera access must respect privacy rules.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm, reading a situation and deciding whether to call the police.

ambition.what: False-alarm causes per zone reviewed every month so sensors and settings get fixed.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the guard closes alarms in the app instead of by radio.

reach.task: Review alarm patterns with the client
reach.learn: Which outcome codes the client needs to act on false alarms.

evidence.claim: Alarm platforms can send events with location data to a mobile dispatch app.
Camera images showing identifiable people are personal data; access for alarm checks needs a set purpose and retention.
Emotion recognition at work and crime prediction based only on profiling are banned AI practices.

assumptions: Boundary: from the alarm signal to the outcome logged; follow-up investigations are outside.

Input contract: alarm zone, time and type from the alarm system; zone maps and key-holder list kept by the security supervisor; outcome code and note entered by the guard in s6; fallback is the radio.
Control room time is outside the guard's savings.
unknowns: Whether the alarm system can push events to an app.
How many alarms per shift are false.
research_questions: Which share of alarms come from a few faulty sensors?

already_counted.description: Guard picks the outcome code and checks the closing note in the app.

incremental.description: Guard reports wrong zone maps or key-holder numbers.
Security supervisor keeps zone maps, key-holder lists and outcome codes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites with long walking distances keep most time in travel and investigation, so the reporting saving is a small share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check and admit visitors and staff at the gate or reception, issue badges and check people out.

steps.what: Visitor arrives at reception and says whom they are visiting
Security guard checks ID and the expected-visitor list from hosts' e-mails
Security guard phones the host to confirm the visit
Host confirms the visit and comes to collect the visitor
Security guard writes the visitor in the visitor book and issues a badge
Security guard monitors employees at the gates and solves badge problems
Security guard checks visitors out, collects badges and checks bags where required

tasks.design: Configure visitor management in the access control system ({OTHER}): hosts pre-register visitors, who get a QR invitation; at reception the guard scans it, checks the ID matches, and the badge prints while the host is notified. Unexpected visitors still go through a host call, and checkout is a badge scan; employee access control is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected visitors were announced by e-mail and logged in a paper book, so each arrival meant searching, calling and writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Visitor management modules with pre-registration, QR codes and badge printing are standard in access control systems.
tasks.still_hard: Hosts forget to pre-register; checking that a person matches their ID and handling unexpected visitors stays manual.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a person's story adds up and refusing entry politely but firmly.

ambition.what: A precise list of who is on site at any moment for evacuations, checked at every drill.

tasks.altitude: The guard spends less time on paperwork and calls and more on watching who comes in.

reach.learn: Whether reception and security can share one visitor flow.

evidence.claim: Visitor management modules support pre-registration, QR invitations and badge printing.
Copying or scanning visitors' ID documents is restricted; checking them is allowed, and visitor data needs a retention period.
Biometric data used to identify a person is special-category data under GDPR, so face recognition at the gate is not assumed.
Remote biometric identification is a high-risk AI area.

assumptions: Boundary: from arrival at the gate to departure; employee badge issuing is outside.
Input contract: visitor pre-registration with name, company, date, host and purpose, produced by the host in the visitor module; fallback is the host call and paper book.
Scenario: about 70% of visitors are pre-registered once hosts are used to it.
Host and visitor time is outside the guard's savings; hosts' pre-registration replaces their confirmation call.
unknowns: Whether the access control system has a visitor module.
How many visitors a day arrive.
research_questions: What share of visitors arrive unannounced after pre-registration is introduced?

already_counted.description: Guard checks that the pre-registration matches the ID shown.

incremental.description: Guard handles visitors whose QR fails or whose host is unreachable.
Facility team keeps host lists and badge printers working.

approvals.approved_version: Visitor name, company and date as confirmed by the host in s4, or in the host's pre-registration; another person or date needs a new confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If only half of hosts pre-register, the guard keeps calling and writing for the rest.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the daily shift report and incident reports on damage, theft, intruders or unusual events, and send them on.

steps.what: Security guard keeps notes of events during the shift
Security guard writes the daily shift report: rounds, alarms, visitors, irregularities
Security guard writes an incident report on theft, damage or unauthorized persons

loop.input: Time-stamped event entries, location codes and photos logged for the incident, and the guard's short notes.
loop.output: A factual incident narrative in the client's report format.
loop.check: Every sentence must cite an entry ID; times, places and names must match entries word for word; a word list flags guesses about motive or guilt; the guard reads and signs.
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most; then the guard writes the narrative.
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative joins free-text notes into readable prose; the template alone only lists entries.

steps.what: Security guard e-mails the shift report to the client contact and the office
Security guard e-mails incident reports to the client contact and the office
Security supervisor reviews incident reports and follows up with the client
Client contact reads the reports and decides on action

tasks.design: Guards log events in a shift app ({OTHER}) as they happen, with time, location code and photo; the shift report is assembled from those entries plus patrol findings, alarm outcomes and visitor counts. For incidents, a bounded model step drafts the narrative from the entries, each sentence tied to an entry; the guard reviews and signs both reports before they are sent to the client.
tasks.previous_blocker: Events lived in notebooks and separate systems, so reports were typed from memory at shift end.
tasks.enabler_now: Shift apps log events with time and place, and language models can draft a narrative that a check ties to logged entries.
tasks.still_hard: Incident reports can end up in police files or court, so wording must stay factual; the guard's own account is still needed.
tasks.human_edge: Describing what they saw clearly and fairly, and knowing what the client must hear today.

ambition.what: A monthly security picture per site for the client, built from the same logged entries.

tasks.altitude: The guard logs as events happen and signs reports instead of writing them; the supervisor follows up from consistent reports.

reach.task: Write incident reports on shop theft
reach.learn: Whether the same entry-linked narrative check fits theft reports.

evidence.claim: Report work can be a records app filled as work happens, with a template assembling the report and a bounded model step drafting the narrative from logged facts, checked sentence by sentence.
Data about suspected criminal offences may be processed only under specific GDPR and national conditions.
Logs per guard can observe performance, so the works council must consent in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Boundary: from events during the shift to reports sent; investigation and client follow-up are outside.

Input contract: event entries with time, location code, type, note and photo, produced by the guard in the shift app; patrol findings, alarm outcomes and visitor log entries produced in their own tasks; fallback is the typed report.
The model runs under the security company's processing agreement; it does not decide guilt or name suspects beyond the entries.
Supervisor and client time is outside the guard's savings.
unknowns: Whether patrol, alarm and visitor data can be read into one report.
research_questions: How often do clients ask for corrections to incident reports today?

already_counted.description: Guard checks the assembled shift report and adds remarks before signing.
Guard checks the drafted incident narrative against entries and photos.

incremental.description: Guard corrects mislogged entries and reports bad drafts.
Security supervisor keeps report templates, location codes and the word list current.

approvals.approved_version: Shift report as checked and signed by the guard in s2; any later entry creates a new version to sign.
Incident report as checked and signed by the guard in s3; any change needs a new signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites without patrol, alarm or visitor apps keep typing those parts of the report, and incident-heavy shifts need more correction of drafts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The guard keeps patrols, alarm response and judging people at the gate; calls, paper books and typed reports shrink.
reach: Facility managers' repair orders from findings
skills_to_grow: Logging events precisely as they happen
Checking drafted reports for facts and fair wording
Using finding and outcome codes consistently
role.ambitious_version: A guard whose logged rounds, alarms and visitors give the client a monthly security picture, with reports signed rather than typed.
